answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to earn harbor clearance through a costly, verifiable deed: before it can trade, an agent must complete a small bonded task whose proof is published for anyone to check. Like a tide that only lets seaworthy boats leave the harbor, this gate makes flooding the ocean of agents with fakes expensive, while honest newcomers pass once and keep their reputation. Cheap copies sink; verified work floats.
